title.narrative: ROAP/THA Thailand Road User Safety Through Technology (TRUST)

description.narrative:
The project “Thailand Road User Safety through Technology (TRUST) Program under the purview of the Overseas Subcommittee of the Tateshina Meeting, established 18 July 2023”, or TRUST, aims to enhance road safety in Thailand and engagement of partners across Japan and Thailand through a collaboration between UN-Habitat, Toyota Mobility Foundation (TMF), Toyota Motors Thailand (TMT), Bangkok Metropolitan Administration (BMA), Asian Institute of Technology (AIT), and other potential counterparts.
The project has 1 expected outcome – EO1: Establish methodology of traffic safety management with data-driven approach by Three-Pronged Approach (man/vehicle/infrastructure) and advocate to Thailand/Global community. The selected pilot cities are Bangkok and Chachoengsao. The duration is expected to be 12 months, tentatively from 28 March 2025 – 27 March 2026, with possibility of extension.
This project will utilize the Tateshina Meeting, an annual meeting between auto 100 industry leaders to discuss partnerships aimed at reaching zero casualties from traffic accidents in Japan in Chino City, Nagano, Through the Overseas Subcommittee, activities are now being explored with a focus on the Asia region, due to its high number of casualties. In Thailand in particular, where accidents involving two-wheeled vehicles account for 80% of traffic casualties, data-driven efforts will be explored with local partners to understand the accident situation, develop countermeasures and promote awareness campaigns. Separated into 2 sub-phases, the first sub-phase 2.1 will facilitate an in-depth study of root causes and countermeasures, while the second sub-phase 2.2 will support scaling the proposed countermeasures with wider stakeholders.
Using proprietary data made available by Toyota through their Driver Monitor Camera (DMC) system, which uses a camera to monitor a driver’s alertness and condition, data is collected in the event data recorder (EDR), which is then analyzed to review driver behavior and incidence of harsh braking. Based upon the research findings in an earlier phase conducted by AIT in Chachoengsao and already tested in 10 road safety hotspots, data collected will be analyzed to help develop a methodology which can be extrapolated to Bangkok context. Finally, this will culminate in a case study to be presented by BMA, TMF, and UN-Habitat at the 2025 International Mayors Forum, while will be taking place between 14-16 October 2025 in Toyota City, Japan.
The project will look at road accidents using the 3-pronged approach – vehicles, people, and traffic infrastructure. It will utilize data and technologies to understand the root causes of road accidents from various road accident databases and collaborating with data partners in Thailand.
Lastly, the project is aligned to Thailand UNSDCF (2022-2026)’s Outcome 2: Human capital needed for social and inclusive development is improved through strengthening institutions, partnerships, and the empowerment of people – Output 3: Improving accessibility, responsiveness and quality of public services as enablers for Thailand’s transformation and Output 4: Enable people with digital literacy, infrastructure and innovation for their inclusion in Thailand’s economic, social and environmental transformation.
